intro_questions.title: Knowledge Questions
intro_questions.description: These questions test your knowledge of MLOps and ML related concepts and principles. We will ask you to answer the same questions again when you have completed the serious game session to measure your learning progress.
intro_questions.question: What is 'concept drift' in the context of Machine Learning?

answers.text: The decline in model accuracy over time due to gradual trends or seasonal changes in real-world data.
The process of a model's underlying code gradually becoming incompatible with updated software libraries.
The intentional shifting of model parameters during training to prevent the gradient from vanishing.
A security vulnerability where an attacker introduces subtle biases into the training set to trigger specific model failures.

intro_questions.question: What is the difference between Machine Learning (ML) and Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) ?

answers.text: ML focuses on model creation and evaluation, while MLOps focuses on the practices and automation of deployment, monitoring, and production maintenance.
ML focuses on the theoretical design and mathematical proofs of algorithms, while MLOps is exclusively concerned with the empirical testing and hyperparameter tuning of those algorithms.
ML handles the initial data exploration and model training, while MLOps manages the one-time transition of the finalized model code to the operations team for permanent deployment.
ML aims to maximize predictive accuracy using isolated datasets, while MLOps prioritizes feature engineering and data augmentation to synthetically improve those datasets.

intro_questions.question: What does the MLOps principle of 'Reproducibility' ensure?

answers.text: That an ML experiment yields identical results whenever it is repeated with the same data and environment.
The ability to trace the lineage of a specific model prediction back to the exact version of the source data and training code.
Ensuring that the model training pipeline can be automatically re-executed whenever there is a significant change in the statistical distribution of input data.
That the model's performance metrics remain consistent across multiple validation datasets.

intro_questions.question: How do the data, training, and deployment pipelines depend on each other in the MLOps lifecycle?

answers.text: They form a feedback loop where monitoring in deployment triggers data re-collection and model retraining.
They execute independently, as the model containerization principle ensures that data engineering, training, and deployment are strictly isolated and do not influence one another.
They are linked through a one-way continuous integration process where the data pipeline feeds the training pipeline.
They operate in parallel and are only synchronized during scheduled batch intervals to ensure that the deployment pipeline serving infrastructure is not disrupted by ongoing training.

intro_questions.question: What impacts could unmanaged pipeline complexity (pipeline jungles) have?

answers.text: It becomes difficult to trace which data version was used to train a deployed model, making it hard to reproduce results or investigate performance drops.
Model finetuning becomes more difficult as hyperparameter search spaces grow with each additional pipeline, ultimately degrading model performance.
The deployment process slows down because each new pipeline step requires approval before it can be connected to the serving layer.
Monitoring becomes harder because alerts are spread across many pipelines, so issues take longer to detect and fix.

intro_questions.question: Based on the descriptions of their roles, which example best illustrates a conflict of interest between an Operational Engineer and a Business Manager?

answers.text: The Operational Engineer wants to delay deployment to add redundancy and improve observability, while the Business Manager pushes to launch immediately to capture a time-sensitive market opportunity
The Operational Engineer wants to reduce operational overhead, while the Business Manager prefers to quickly support different product variants.

The Operational Engineer advocates for stricter data validation checks that may occasionally block data ingestion, while the Business Manager wants uninterrupted data flow to ensure dashboards are always up to date
The Operational Engineer wants to optimize infrastructure costs by reducing overprovisioning, while the Business Manager wants predictable performance during peak demand periods

intro_questions.question: In the context of MLOps stakeholder roles, what is the primary distinction between the responsibilities of a Data Scientist and an MLOps Engineer?

answers.text: Data Scientists focus on algorithm selection, model development, and evaluation, while MLOps Engineers focus on integrating and optimizing the pipelines designed by Data Scientists and Data Engineers.
Data Scientists ensure the scalability of data operations and manage feature storage, while MLOps Engineers handle the classical CI/CD automation and workflow orchestration.
Data Scientists focus on the initial data collection and filtering processes, while MLOps Engineers are primarily responsible for designing the overall system architecture and monitoring paradigms.

Data Scientists assess the feasibility of machine learning solutions alongside domain experts, while MLOps Engineers manage the storage infrastructure and acquire new data sources for model retraining.
